findings.statement: CA9 has one transmembrane segment and 377 extracellular residues, suitability 0.647 (rank 13 of 2017), but the Human Protein Atlas shows staining level 3.0 in stomach (a vital organ) and 0.0 in kidney; in the weakest quarter of donors only 24.3 percent of tumour cells express it (median donor 53.3). It is a known target (control), and the score does not show a conjugate would work.

CD70 has the best ADC suitability among the controls, 0.746 (rank 2 of 2017), with 155 extracellular residues; 17.7 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors (median donor 41.2). Vital-organ staining data were not available (staining_data_available false), so normal-tissue safety is untested here.

ENPP3 has suitability 0.578 (rank 39 of 2017); staining is 3.0 in duodenum and 3.0 in kidney, which is a liability for an on-target toxicity; 21.3 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors (median donor 31.0). Known target used as a control.

SCARB1, top of the target ranking, has suitability 0.558 (rank 51 of 2017), two transmembrane segments, staining 3.0 in adrenal gland and 2.0 in kidney, and only 7.1 percent of tumour cells expressing it in the weakest quarter of donors (median donor 12.4). It is not a known ADC target; broad normal expression and sparse tumour-cell coverage argue against a conjugate.

SLC16A3 has suitability 0.725 (rank 3 of 2017) and the highest weakest-quarter tumour coverage, 43.7 percent (median donor 49.4), but it spans the membrane 12 times with only 66 extracellular residues and stains 3.0 in adrenal gland and 2.0 in kidney. A small-molecule inhibitor may be more realistic than a conjugate; this is a score, not proof.

CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit but not significantly in any arm: atezolizumab plus bevacizumab log HR -0.112 per SD (padj 0.665, n 88), sunitinib -0.336 (padj 0.332, n 89), atezolizumab -0.212 (padj 0.68, n 86); the arm difference is 0.224 (padj 0.779). It is a lead at most, not a predictor.

Higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log HR -0.383 per SD, padj 0.166, n 88) and on sunitinib (-0.262, padj 0.434, n 89); the difference between arms is -0.121 (padj 0.927). Nothing passes correction, so this stays a lead from a single 88-patient arm.

PCK1 (down in tumours) is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log HR 0.22 per SD, padj 0.572, n 88) and slightly longer benefit on sunitinib (-0.069, padj 0.889, n 89); the arm difference is 0.289 (padj 0.754). Not significant.

For NNMT the tool returned only the 16-patient nivolumab trial: log HR 0.34 per SD (padj 0.782), direction earlier progression with higher expression. This is direction only with n 16 and cannot support any claim; no IMmotion150 arm values were returned.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation (CPTAC RNA +0.971, padj 0.014; CPTAC protein +0.335, padj 0.067; TCGA RNA +1.148, padj 7.18e-7), and it is lower in ccB than ccA (TCGA RNA -1.551, padj 1.06e-9). The protein difference is not significant at 0.05, so the subgroup call rests mainly on RNA.

PSAT1 is not a subgroup target candidate for any of VHL, PBRM1, BAP1, SETD2, but is higher in ccB than ccA (TCGA RNA +2.364, padj 9.07e-39; CPTAC protein +0.541, padj 0.0000157). BAP1 mutants have higher RNA (TCGA +1.711, padj 0.0000578) but not protein (CPTAC +0.224, padj 0.396).

NNMT does not differ meaningfully by VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 status (for example PBRM1 TCGA RNA +0.347, padj 0.064) nor between ccB and ccA (TCGA RNA -0.044, padj 0.82). It is a pan-subtype tumour marker, not a subgroup-specific target.

Immune cells account for 0.654 of CD70 tumour transcripts, with Spearman correlation to CD8 T cells 0.278, regulatory T cells 0.228, M2 macrophages -0.004 and immune score 0.196 (immune-target score 3.384, rank 20 of 19161). A large part of the signal is immune, so tumour-cell-restricted targeting is not guaranteed; log HR on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is -0.383.

FCGR3A is almost entirely immune: 0.999 of its tumour transcripts come from immune cells, with correlation to CD8 T cells 0.457, M2 macrophages 0.361 and immune score 0.795 (score 3.499, rank 13 of 19161). Its tumour increase (RNA log2FC 3.51) reflects infiltration, not tumour-cell expression.

NNMT attribution holds in the second single-cell dataset: dominant group RCC in both Li 2022 and Zhang 2021, tumour-cell share 0.97 and 0.948, tumour vs proximal tubule log2FC 9.132 and 5.573 (share-profile Spearman 0.786; 4 paired donors).

SLC16A3 cell attribution does not hold: dominant group T_NK in Li 2022 (tumour-cell share 0.327) but RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.809); tumour vs tubule log2FC is 6.809 and 6.45. Its tumour increase is reproducible, but whether tumour cells or T/NK cells carry it is unresolved.

CD70 cell call is discordant: T_NK dominant in Li 2022 (tumour-cell share 0.345) versus RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.964); tumour vs tubule log2FC 6.899 and 5.281. This agrees with its high immune transcript share and calls for caution as a tumour-cell target.

CA9 is tumour-cell dominant in both datasets (RCC; tumour-cell share 0.976 in Li 2022 and 0.981 in Zhang 2021), tumour vs tubule log2FC 7.739 and 8.522 (share-profile Spearman 0.607; 4 paired donors).

PSAT1 protein replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort: log2FC -3.946 (padj 9.71e-23, 69 pairs) versus -1.963 in discovery. Its one measured phosphosite was significant in discovery but did not replicate (0 replicating).
NNMT protein replicates: confirmatory log2FC 4.776 (padj 3.07e-46, 86 pairs) versus 2.709 in discovery. Absolute sizes differ by technology; direction and significance agree.
SCARB1 protein replicates: confirmatory log2FC 2.334 (padj 3.28e-10, 33 pairs) versus 1.837 in discovery.
PCK1 protein loss replicates: confirmatory log2FC -4.819 (padj 3.53e-27, 69 pairs) versus -1.859 in discovery, and 2 of 2 measured phosphosites replicate.

caveats: IMmotion150 results are single-gene leads from arms of about 88 patients; none differs between arms after correction, so all are only 'associated with'.
For NNMT, SCARB1 and EPAS1 the treatment tool returned only the 16-patient nivolumab trial (direction only, e.g. EPAS1 log HR -0.236, padj 0.88).
A high ADC suitability score does not show a conjugate would work; CD70 has no vital-organ staining data, and CA9, ENPP3, SCARB1 and SLC16A3 show strong staining in vital organs or kidney.
CA9 and CD70 were not tested in the confirmatory proteomics cohort (fewer than 10 matched pairs); this is missing data, not a failed replication.
Only some of the requested genes (for example EPAS1, PSAT1 ADC and immune layers) were profiled in every layer within the call budget.
PSAT1, PCK1 and other tumour-down genes rank high on the biomarker profile; they are loss markers and not drug targets.
